title: Exchange of driving licenses with Australia to start October 31
text:
The Australian transportation authority Austroads announced on July 23 that Taiwan had been included in its Recognised Overseas Licenses Scheme. Individuals holding valid Taiwan automobile or motorcycle licenses may, subject to the regulations of individual Australian states and territories, exchange their document for an Australian license without needing to take a written exam or a road test. The policy is expected to take effect as early as October 31, starting in Western Australia and Queensland.

Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung welcomes and affirms this outcome, which the result of the efforts of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) and the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office in Australia. Moving forward, MOFA will work with the Ministry of Transportation and Communications to ensure that, based on the principle of reciprocity, Australian citizens in Taiwan are granted equivalent treatment.

The implementation schedule released by Australia for those wishing to exchange a valid Taiwan automobile or motorcycle license is as follows:

October 31, 2026: Western Australia and Queensland

January 1, 2027: New South Wales, South Australia, Northern Territory

February 1, 2027: Tasmania

No timetable has yet been set for the Australian Capital Territory or Victoria.

Important notes:

1. As states and territories are implementing the policy at different times, individuals should apply in line with the regulations of their place of residence and refer to announcements made by the local transportation authority.

2. While the arrangement permits an exchange of licenses without the need for a written or road test, applicants must still abide by local regulations concerning identity, age, health, validity period of their existing license, and other matters.

3. The arrangement primarily concerns passenger vehicles and motorcycles; for other types of vehicles, the regulations of the relevant Australian state or territory will apply.

MOFA and TECO Australia and its branch offices will continue to track the implementation of this policy by Australian states and territories. They will remain in contact with the relevant Australian authorities and provide needed updates so as to protect the rights, interests, and convenience of holders of Taiwan driving licenses in Australia.
